evidence: Flask app structure with clearly separated modules (app/auth, app/main, app/api) grouped by domain/function rather than technical layer
No inter-process communication; all components run in same process and share in-memory state
Use of Blueprints for modular routing and concerns, indicating internal modularity within a single deployable unit
Shared database access via SQLAlchemy ORM, with models in app/models.py
Configurable environment-specific setups (config.py) without external service boundaries
Tests co-located in tests/ directory alongside application code, typical of monolithic test strategy
Avg fan-out of ~3.4 and max directory depth of 3 suggest moderate coupling within a single codebase
No evidence of bounded contexts, external adapters, or service boundaries typical of microservices/hexagonal
risks: Tight integration may complicate scaling or team independence over time
Changes in core modules (e.g., models.py) may ripple across many modules
Deployment and recovery are tied to monolithic release cycles
